intents.intent: Title a page, with its actions
intents.emits: `header` with `h1`, subtitle and an action slot
`label` + help and error lines the caller binds by id
`div` with a finite CSS entrance, none under reduced motion
the shared consent stylesheet and script; a product adapter mounts it ([`../design-system/consent-footer.md`](../design-system/consent-footer.md))
`table` in a focusable scroll region, total in `tfoot`

props.name: autofocus
props.docs: Takes first focus when its modal [`crate::Dialog`] opens.

example.code: Button { size: Size::Small, onclick: move |_| elapsed += 15, "+15s" }

components.name: LinkButton
components.docs:
An anchor styled as a button.

A call-to-action that navigates is an `<a>`, not a `<button>` — it must be
middle-clickable, openable in a new tab, and crawlable. This crate takes
`dioxus` without the router feature so the kit stays renderer-agnostic;
callers pass a plain `href` and wrap with `Link` themselves if they want
client-side routing.

props.name: external
props.docs:
Set for links leaving the site; adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, without
which the opened page can reach back through `window.opener`.

props.name: download
props.docs:
The `download` filename, for a link that saves a file rather than
opening a page.

props.name: disabled
props.docs:
Renders the link with no `href`.

`pointer-events: none` alone, which is what the hand-written version
did, stops a mouse and nothing else: the link stays in the tab order and
Enter still follows it. An anchor without an `href` is not focusable and
cannot be followed at all, which is what "disabled" has to mean.

example.code: LinkButton { href: "/#pricing", size: Size::Large, "Get started" }

guarantees.docs:
The export link this replaced was `pointer-events: none`, which stops a
mouse and nothing else — it stayed in the tab order and Enter followed it.

components.name: TextLink
components.docs:
An inline, underlined link that inherits its type size from the text around
it.

props.name: external
props.docs: Opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

props.name: strong
props.docs: The link is the subject of its line, not a route off it.

example.code: TextLink { href: "https://example.com", external: true, "Elsewhere" }

components.name: ArrowLink
components.docs:
Inline "Read more →" link.

The arrow is `aria-hidden` — it is decoration, and a screen reader reading
"rightwards arrow" after every link is noise.

example.code: ArrowLink { href: "/#how-it-works", "See how it works" }

props.name: name
props.docs:
The `name` attribute.

Optional, but omitting it is half of what made the login screen a form
that could not submit anything: a native form POST serializes fields
**by name**, and a nameless input contributes nothing to the body at
all. Password managers key on it too — without one they cannot offer to
save or fill a credential.

props.name: autocomplete
props.docs:
The `autocomplete` token — `email`, `current-password`, and so on.

A fixed vocabulary, not free text. Browsers need it to fill credentials
into the right box.

props.name: error
props.docs:
Field-level validation message. Rendered with `role="alert"` so screen
readers announce it — a validation error nobody hears is not a
validation error.

example.code: TextField { label: "Name", value: note(), oninput: move |e: FormEvent| note.set(e.value()) }

guarantees.docs: Two of the four hand-made inputs this replaced had no focus ring.

A nameless input contributes nothing to a native form submission, which is
half of how the login screen once shipped unable to submit.

a2ui.name: value
a2ui.docs: Where the input reads and writes.

components.name: Select
components.docs:
A labelled select.

`options` is `(value, label)` because the value is what goes in a URL and
the label is what a person reads, and the two are never the same string once
the copy is written in plain English.

components.name: Input
components.docs:
A bare text control, for a field whose label is not a line of text above it
— a search box labelled for screen readers only, a free-text answer under a
question that is already its label.

[`TextField`] is this inside a [`FieldShell`], so the field styling has one
home. Apps had been copying it by hand, and two of the four copies dropped
the focus ring.

props.name: name
props.docs: The `name` attribute. See [`TextField`] for why a form needs it.

props.name: autocomplete
props.docs: The `autocomplete` token — `email`, `current-password`, `off`.

props.name: describedby
props.docs:
Space-separated IDs of the messages describing this control; see
[`field_description`].

props.name: invalid
props.docs: `aria-invalid`. `None` omits the attribute.

props.name: class
props.docs: Layout only: room for an adornment inside the box, say.

example.code: Input { id: "q", value: "", oninput: |_| {} }

guarantees.docs: Two of the four hand-made inputs this replaced had no focus ring.

A nameless input contributes nothing to a native form submission, which is
half of how the login screen once shipped unable to submit.

components.name: CommandSelect
components.docs:
Controlled single selection. `id` must be unique within the page.

Options use stable `(value, label)` pairs. Filtering never changes the
selected value; only an explicit option selection calls `onchange`.

components.name: Checkbox
components.docs:
A labelled checkbox, optionally carrying a count of what it would match.

The count is the reason this is a component rather than a bare `input`. A
filter rail that shows a facet with no count forces the reader to click it
to discover it matches nothing, and a rail whose zero-count options vanish
makes the list flicker as selections change. Showing the number, and dimming
rather than hiding a zero, keeps the set of options stable while still
saying which ones are worth choosing.

props.name: count
props.docs:
How many records this option would match right now. Rendered to the
right, dimmed when nought.

props.name: basis
props.docs:
Where the value came from, when it was derived rather than recorded —
"headcount band, not revenue". Shown under the label and bound as the
box's description, so the reader can disagree with a judgement the data
did not actually make. A `title` would hide it from touch and most
screen readers.

example.code: Checkbox { label: "Mid-size", checked: false, count: 4, basis: "headcount band, not revenue", onchange: |_| {} }

components.name: FieldSet
components.docs:
A group of controls under a legend, with the count of how many are on.

`native` fieldset and legend rather than a styled div: a screen reader
announces the legend with every control inside it, which is the only thing
that tells someone tabbing through thirty checkboxes which group they are
in.

props.name: note
props.docs:
A sentence under the legend saying what the group does, for a group
whose meaning is not obvious from its title alone.

props.name: active
props.docs: How many controls in this group are switched on.

components.name: Card
components.docs:
A bordered surface.

Flat by default, with no shadow. Every hand-made surface it replaced was
flat, and a product that spends a shadow on meaning — one verdict that must
stand out — cannot do so if every card already casts one. [`Surface::Slab`]
is that one.

`class` is for layout inside the card: flex direction, gaps, alignment.

a2ui.name: children
a2ui.docs: Ids of the components inside, in order.

a2ui.name: surface
a2ui.docs: flat: hairline border. slab: ink border and offset shadow.

components.name: Section
components.docs:
A page section with consistent vertical padding.

Takes an optional `id` so a nav link can target it — an in-page anchor is
the cheapest navigation a marketing site has, and it needs no router.

components.name: Container
components.docs:
Centred, padded content column.

`class` is for layout inside the column — flex direction, gaps, vertical
padding — never for its width, which is what [`Width`] is for.

components.name: Grid
components.docs:
Responsive column grid.

Collapses to a single column on small screens in every case; `columns` is
the widest arrangement, not a fixed one.

a2ui.name: children
a2ui.docs: Ids of the components inside, in order.

components.name: Divider
components.docs:
Horizontal rule.

`aria-hidden` because it is decoration; a screen reader announcing
"separator" between every section is noise.

example.code: Divider {}

components.name: Disclosure
components.docs:
A native `details`/`summary` disclosure.

Native rather than a signal and a conditional render, because the browser
already gives this keyboard operation, the right ARIA state and find-in-page
that reaches inside a closed section. A hand-rolled one gives up all three.

props.name: accent
props.docs:
A CSS colour for a left rule down the open body, used where the
disclosure carries a graded judgement rather than plain detail.

components.name: Faq
components.docs:
Expandable FAQ list.

Built on native `<details>`/`<summary>`, which gives correct expand/collapse
semantics, keyboard operation and in-page find with **zero JavaScript** —
so it works in the SSG build before (or without) hydration. A hand-rolled
accordion would need state, an effect, and `aria-expanded` wiring to reach
the same place.

components.name: Heading
components.docs:
A heading at an explicit semantic level.

`level` drives the tag, `size` drives the appearance. Defaulting `level` to
2 is deliberate: a page has exactly one `<h1>`, and it is almost always the
hero, so every other heading opting into 2 is the safer default.

example.code: Heading { "Figures that arrive" }

components.name: Text
components.docs: A paragraph of body copy.

components.name: Eyebrow
components.docs:
Small uppercase label above a heading. Rendered as a `

`, not a heading: it is a visual lead-in, and promoting it to `

` would put a meaningless entry in the document outline.

example.code: Eyebrow { "Default theme" }

components.name: PageHeader
components.intent: Title a page, with its actions
components.emits: `header` with `h1`, subtitle and an action slot

components.name: FieldShell
components.emits: `label` + help and error lines the caller binds by id
components.docs: Labels a custom control whose ID and description attributes the caller binds.

components.name: StepMarker
components.docs:
The `01` / `02` / `03` marker used by feature cards and step lists.

Zero-padded to two digits so the markers stay optically aligned past nine.

components.name: PageEntrance
components.emits: `div` with a finite CSS entrance, none under reduced motion
components.docs: Opt-in finite page entrance. Reduced-motion users receive no animation.

example.code: PageEntrance { {children} }

components.name: ConsentFooter
components.emits: the shared consent stylesheet and script; a product adapter mounts it ([`../design-system/consent-footer.md`](../design-system/consent-footer.md))
components.docs:
Loads the shared browser renderer for SSG and hydrated product adapters.
Mount after `rv2-consent-ready`, or immediately when `window.Rv2ConsentFooter` exists.

example.code: ConsentFooter {}

components.name: Badge
components.docs: Small pill label.

props.name: colour
props.docs:
A CSS colour this badge takes for its text and border, instead of a fill.

Exists so a set of badges can encode a category rather than merely
label it. A reader scanning a long list sees the colour before they
read the word, which is the whole reason a category has a colour.

example.code: Badge { fill: BadgeFill::Tint, "12" }

components.name: Status
components.docs:
How healthy something is, as a dot plus its label.

The dot is what makes a column of these scannable; the label is what makes
it readable when the dot is invisible to you. Both, always — a colour on its
own is not a status anyone can act on.

components.name: Swatch
components.docs:
A small filled circle carrying a category's colour.

Sits beside a filter option so the rail and the results agree visually: the
swatch next to "FTSE 250" is the same green as the badge on every FTSE 250
company.

components.name: Bar
components.docs:
One labelled row of a proportional bar chart.

The number is always rendered as text and the bar sits behind it. That
order is deliberate: the bar is the thing a reader scans and the number is
the thing they act on, so the number can never be the part that got
estimated from a pixel width. A reader with the bar hidden — a screen
reader, a high-contrast mode, a printout — loses nothing.

`of` is the largest count in the set rather than the total, because the
question these answer is "which of these is biggest" far more often than
"what share of the whole is this". A bar scaled to a total where one bucket
holds 95% is six invisible slivers and one full bar.

props.name: of
props.docs: The largest count in the set, which sets the full width.

props.name: colour
props.docs:
A CSS colour for the fill, where the category already has one the reader
knows.

props.name: emphasis
props.docs: Whether this row is one the reader is hunting for.

example.code: Bar { label: "Remote", count: 92, of: 120, arrive: Arrive::Grow }

components.name: EmptyState
components.docs:
Shown when a collection is legitimately empty — as distinct from loading
(use [`Skeleton`]) or failed (use [`ErrorBanner`]). Conflating the three is
the most common way a list UI lies to the user.

example.code: Skeleton { lines: 4 }
ErrorBanner { message }

components.name: ProductHeader
components.docs:
Stable product header with route state and a native mobile disclosure.

Navigation uses plain URLs to keep this crate router-neutral. Browser apps
may use these links as deliberate full navigations or keep router-specific
navigation outside this component.

example.code:
ProductHeader {
    brand: PUBLIC_PRODUCT_NAME,
    brand_href: PUBLIC_SITE_URL,
    brand_subtitle: "Application",
    items: vec![
        NavLink::route("dashboard", "Dashboard", "/"),
        NavLink::route("posts", "Posts", "/posts"),
        NavLink::route("runway", "Runway", "/runway"),
    ],
    current,
    tail,
}

guarantees.docs:
The desktop tail is `display: none` on narrow screens, so a sign-out placed
there would be unreachable on a phone unless the mobile menu carries it too.

components.name: NavigationRail
components.docs: Compact route, policy, or article index.

components.name: ProcessRail
components.docs:
Ordered process with optional current-step semantics.

`active_step` is one-based. Omit it for a static process explanation.

components.name: Tabs
components.docs:
A tab list whose current value belongs to the caller.

`label` names the group for a screen reader. Without it the list announces
as an unlabelled set of tabs, which says what the control is but not what it
switches.

`controls` is the `id` of the element the tabs switch, and it is required
rather than optional: a tab list referencing no panel announces as a set of
buttons that change nothing. The caller marks that element `role="tabpanel"`
and points its `aria-labelledby` at `tab-{value}`.

components.name: Footer
components.docs: Site footer.

props.name: note
props.docs: Attribution or copyright line.

components.name: Hero
components.docs:
Above-the-fold headline block.

The heading is a literal `<h1>` — a marketing page has exactly one, and it
belongs here.

props.name: actions
props.docs: Call-to-action row.

props.name: media
props.docs: Illustration or screenshot, rendered beside the copy on wide screens.

components.name: FeatureCard
components.docs: Numbered card in a feature grid.

props.name: action
props.docs: Trailing link, e.g. an `ArrowLink`.

components.name: StepList
components.docs:
Ordered "how it works" list.

A real `<ol>`: the order carries meaning, and the numbers are generated by
[`StepMarker`] from the index so they can never drift out of sequence when
a step is inserted.

components.name: FactList
components.docs:
Itemised figures.

A `<dl>` rather than a `<table>`: these are name/value pairs, not tabular
data with meaningful rows *and* columns. Values are `tabular-nums` so
digits align down the column.

components.name: PricingCard
components.docs: One-off or subscription price block.

components.name: PressButton
components.docs:
A button that rests on a ledge, lifts on hover and presses down on click.

The icon tilts on hover and on keyboard focus alike, so the affordance a
mouse user sees is not withheld from a keyboard user.

props.name: icon
props.docs: Image URL for a decorative leading icon.

example.code: PressButton { press: Press::Offset, class: "mt-4", "Send the card" }

components.name: PressLink
components.docs: [`PressButton`]'s look on an anchor, for a call-to-action that navigates.

props.name: external
props.docs: Opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

example.code: PressLink { href: "#cards", icon: STAR_ICON.to_string(), "Find an activity" }

components.name: SaveToggle
components.docs:
A save/unsave toggle whose gem pulses each time it is pressed.

The pulse restarts on every press, including two in quick succession: the
animation alternates between two identical keyframe names, because a CSS
animation that keeps the same name does not replay when its class is
re-applied.

State is the caller's: `saved` in, `ontoggle` with the next value out.

props.name: icon
props.docs: Image URL for the gem; a heart glyph when absent.

components.name: ChipGroup
components.docs:
A labelled row of [`Chip`]s.

`role="group"` with a name, so a screen reader announces "Filter
activities, group" before the first chip rather than a run of unexplained
toggles.

components.name: Chip
components.docs:
One selectable filter chip. `active` is exposed as `aria-pressed`, not as
colour alone.

components.name: MediaCard
components.docs:
A browsing card: a picture that eases forward on hover, a category line, a
linked title, a body and actions pinned to the bottom.

The picture and the title are two links to one place. The picture link is
named by `title` and taken out of the tab order, so a keyboard user tabs
once per card rather than twice.

guarantees.docs: Two links per card would double every keyboard user's tab stops.

components.name: Masthead
components.docs:
A newspaper masthead: a strap line, the wordmark, a subtitle, and a nav
between a double rule and a single one.

For a site whose identity is editorial — a gazette, a desk, a journal —
where [`crate::ProductHeader`]'s sticky app bar would read as software.

props.name: mark
props.docs: Image URL for a mark set beside the wordmark.

props.name: strap
props.docs:
Left and right of the strap above the wordmark; the right one is
dropped on narrow screens.

example.code:
Masthead {
    brand: "The Play Desk",
    mark: STAR_ICON.to_string(),
    subtitle: "Tactile controls, in the palette they were drawn in",
    strap: ("rv2-ui · tactile".to_string(), "Theme: playful".to_string()),
    items: vec![
        NavLink::route("press", "Buttons", "#press"),
        NavLink::route("chips", "Chips", "#chips"),
        NavLink::route("cards", "Cards", "#cards"),
    ],
    current: "press",
}

components.name: Sparkle
components.docs:
A four-point star that unfolds once when it mounts. Decoration only; place
it inside a `position: relative` parent.

example.code: Sparkle {}

components.name: StatStrip
components.docs:
A row of headline figures between rules, collapsing to two columns on a
narrow screen.

A `dl`, so each figure is announced with its label rather than as a bare
number.

a2ui.name: density
a2ui.docs: compact: a summary row. hero: the band the page is about.

components.name: ResultPanel
components.docs:
A calculator's answer: a kicker row, one large figure, and the working
beneath it (a [`crate::FactList`], usually).

The figure is `aria-live="polite"`, so a screen reader hears the new answer
when an input changes it, without being interrupted mid-sentence. The
working is outside the live region: re-reading it on every keystroke
buries the answer.

props.name: context
props.docs: The right side of the kicker: the period, the basis, the date.

a2ui.name: value
a2ui.docs: The figure, as text, with its sign and unit.

a2ui.name: lean
a2ui.docs: Whether the figure is good news.

components.name: Meter
components.docs:
How far along something is against its limit, coloured by threshold.

`role="meter"` with its value and range, so the number is available to a
screen reader that cannot see the fill.

props.name: readout
props.docs:
The text shown for the value — `"412 of 500 runs"`. The fill never
carries the number alone.

props.name: warn_at
props.docs: From this share of `max` the fill turns to caution.

props.name: critical_at
props.docs: From this share of `max` the fill turns to fault.

props.name: ticks
props.docs:
Draws this many equal ticks across the track, for a quantity counted in
whole portions — doses, slots, sections.

example.code: Meter { label: "Monthly budget", value: 212.0, max: 250.0, readout: "£212 of £250", warn_at: 0.8, critical_at: 0.95, ticks: 10 }

a2ui.name: readout
a2ui.docs: The amount in words, shown beside the fill.

a2ui.name: warnAt
a2ui.docs: Share of max from which the fill shows caution.

a2ui.name: criticalAt
a2ui.docs: Share of max from which the fill shows fault.

components.name: SplitBar
components.docs:
A whole split into its parts — energy against fees, principal against
interest — as one bar with a legend that carries every figure.

[`crate::Bar`] compares many things to the biggest of them; this shows what
one thing is made of.

With [`crate::Arrive::Grow`] the parts settle left to right, so the bar
reads as one whole filling once.

components.name: Callout
components.docs:
A boxed aside with a coloured edge: a verdict strip, a "what this does not
cover" note, a missing-evidence warning.

`title` is the verdict in words, so the edge colour is never the only
signal. A `Stop` is announced as an alert.

example.code: Callout { verdict: Verdict::Clear, title: "Applies", "The offer clears the floor by £38." }

a2ui.name: verdict
a2ui.docs: What the callout is telling the reader. stop is announced as an alert.

components.name: Receipt
components.docs:
The record of something done: a status in mono capitals, a grid of facts,
a note and what to do next.

props.name: status
props.docs: The state in a word or two — `SENT`, `DRAFT`, `PAID`.

props.name: facts
props.docs: `(term, value)` rows.

components.name: UnitField
components.docs:
A labelled number with its unit fused into the box: `£ [ 1,200 ]`,
`[ 7.4 ] kW`, `[ 3 ] hours`.

The ring is on the shell (`focus-within`), not the input, so the unit is
inside the focused control rather than beside it. The affixes are
`aria-hidden` because the label names the unit; give the label the unit
("Charger power, kW") for a screen reader to hear it.

props.name: inputmode
props.docs:
The on-screen keyboard: `decimal` for money and measures, `numeric`
for whole counts.

example.code: UnitField { label: "Price per kWh, pence", value: price(), suffix: "p/kWh", oninput: move |e: FormEvent| price.set(e.value()) }

a2ui.name: label
a2ui.docs: The label; name the unit here for screen readers.

a2ui.name: value
a2ui.docs: Where the input reads and writes.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.docs:
A joined row of mutually exclusive options that narrows what is shown: a
list/map view, monthly/yearly prices, a scope.

Not [`crate::Tabs`]: tabs switch between panels, this filters one. Buttons
with `aria-pressed` inside a named group, the same contract as
[`crate::Chip`].

props.name: options
props.docs: `(value, label)`.

example.code:
SegmentedControl {
    label: "Tone",
    options: vec![("plain".into(), "Plain and direct".into()), ("warm".into(), "Warm and brief".into()), ("formal".into(), "Formal".into())],
    value: tone(),
    onchange: move |next| tone.set(next),
    flow: SegmentFlow::StackNarrow,
}

components.name: ChoiceGroup
components.docs:
Mutually exclusive options as cards, each a title and a line saying what
choosing it means.

Native radios in a fieldset, so arrow keys move between options and a
screen reader announces the legend and the position. The selected card is
drawn from `:has(:checked)`, never a second copy of the state. Drawn from
Move to Own's action options, Logo Handoff's context choice and Reefdose's
parameter grid. [`SegmentedControl`] is the compact form for short labels.

props.name: name
props.docs: The radios' shared `name`; unique on the page.

example.code:
ChoiceGroup {
    legend: "How the cost is split",
    name: "kit-plan",
    choices: plan_cards,
    value: plan(),
    onchange: move |next| plan.set(next),
}

components.name: Dialog
components.docs:
A modal dialog over the page.

The caller owns `open` and hears every request to change it through
`on_open_change`: Escape, the close button and a click on the backdrop all
ask rather than close. Keep the component mounted while closed and its
children keep their drafts.

`alert` makes it an `alertdialog`, for a decision the reader must answer.
A focusable child with `autofocus` takes first focus; otherwise the browser
focuses the first focusable element.

props.name: dismissible
props.docs:
`false` while a pending action must not be abandoned: Escape, the
backdrop and the close button stop asking to close.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.docs:
A destructive decision in an `alertdialog`.

First focus is the least destructive action. While `pending` it cannot be
dismissed and the confirm button is busy; on failure it stays open with
`error` shown, so the reader is never left guessing whether it happened.

components.name: ArmedDeleteButton
components.docs:
Delete in two clicks without a dialog: the first arms it and changes its
label, the second confirms.

For a row action where a modal would be heavier than the loss. The caller
owns `armed`. Escape and leaving the button disarm it, and nothing confirms
while `busy` or `disabled`. Screen readers do not reliably re-read a focused
button whose label changes, so a status beside it speaks the armed label.

components.name: ToastProvider
components.docs: Mount once above everything that raises a toast.

components.name: Toaster
components.docs:
Where toasts render. Mount once, inside the [`ToastProvider`].

A named `region` landmark rather than a live region: each toast carries its
own `alert` or `status`, and a live container would announce it twice.

example.code: Toaster {}

components.name: Stamp
components.docs:
A square outline tag in capitals: `OPEN`, `READY`, `VOID`.

Reads as a rubber stamp on a record rather than a pill on a list, which is
the difference from [`crate::Badge`]. The word carries the verdict; the
colour repeats it.

example.code: Stamp { verdict: Verdict::Caution, "Open" }

a2ui.name: verdict
a2ui.docs: The colour that repeats the word.

components.name: GateList
components.docs:
A readiness checklist: each row a glyph, a label and why.

The glyph is hidden from assistive technology and its meaning is spoken as
text instead, so the state never rests on a shape or a colour. Drawn from
the control room's gate rows, Logo Handoff's asset rows and Reefdose's
verification grid.

components.name: RedlineDiff
components.docs:
What an edit changed, as struck and inserted text per field.

Most screen readers do not announce `del` and `ins`, so each side starts
with a visually hidden "Removed:" or "Added:"; the elements still carry it
in a printout and the colours repeat it. Drawn from Edit Scope's draft
receipt.

components.name: CompareTable
components.docs:
Options side by side, a row per feature.

A real `table` on wide screens. Below `sm` each option's cells stack as a
card and every cell prints its column's name from `data-label`, so nothing
scrolls sideways and no cell loses its heading. Drawn from A Place Ahead's
comparison, All Source's pricing matrix and Move to Own's responsive table.

props.name: columns
props.docs: The header of the row-label column, then one per option.

props.name: highlight
props.docs:
Index into the options (not counting the label column) to set apart:
the recommended plan, the reader's current choice.

components.name: Tally
components.docs:
A whole number that counts up to itself as it scrolls into view.

It takes the size and weight of whatever text it sits in. The number is
text, so nothing reads the figure out of a counter. `assets/arrive.css`
hides that text visually and draws a CSS counter, hidden from assistive
technology, in its place; a page without the stylesheet shows the text.

A CSS counter holds a signed 32-bit integer, so the visible digits stop at
`i32::MAX`; the text copy is always exact.

example.code: Tally { value: 174 }

components.name: Sparkline
components.docs:
The trend of `values`, stretched to its container's width.

Decorative unless `label` is given, in which case it is an image with that
name — "Resting heart rate, falling over 6 weeks". A named series that
cannot be drawn shows its name as text, so the trend is not lost with the
line. The stroke colour is the `--rv2-spark-stroke` hook.

example.code: Sparkline { values: vec![61.0, 60.0, 62.0, 59.0, 58.0, 57.0], label: "Resting heart rate, falling over 6 weeks" }

components.name: LedgerTable
components.emits: `table` in a focusable scroll region, total in `tfoot`
components.docs:
Records as rows: transactions, a quote's lines, a schedule.

The first cell of each row is its row header. A `total` goes in `tfoot`, so
it is never read as one more record. Callers render an [`crate::EmptyState`]
themselves when there are no rows; the table owns no copy.

props.name: caption_hidden
props.docs:
Keeps the caption for assistive technology and hides it on screen,
where a heading above already names the table.

props.name: action_label
props.docs: The header of the trailing action column, when any row has an action.

components.name: Citation
components.docs:
Where a figure came from and when: "Checked 24 Sep 2026 · Open Ofsted ↗".

The kit has no date library, so the caller passes the date twice: ISO for
`datetime` and as the reader should see it.

example.code: Citation { source: "the school's inspection report", date_iso: "2026-09-24", date_text: "24 Sep 2026", dated: Dated::Checked, href: "https://reports.ofsted.gov.uk/" }

components.name: AttentionQueue
components.docs:
The queue. The caller supplies the heading; the list is named by `label`.

Item ids key the rows and must be unique; a repeated id makes Dioxus reuse
the wrong row's DOM, so debug builds panic on one.

A `Go` row is one link with a real `href`. `on_open` lets an app route on
the client and still leaves the `href` for a new tab or no script.

props.name: empty
props.docs: Shown instead of the list when it is empty.

props.name: numbered
props.docs: Prints 01, 02… beside each row for a queue read by position.

components.name: Popover
components.docs:
A panel opened by a button, on the native `popover` attribute.

The browser supplies light dismiss, Escape, one-open-at-a-time and the top
layer, and exposes the trigger's expanded state, so none of it is scripted.
Where CSS anchor positioning is supported the panel sits under its trigger;
elsewhere the browser centres it, which is still usable.

`id` names the panel and its anchor, so it must be a valid CSS identifier.

props.name: label
props.docs:
The trigger's accessible name. Required, because a trigger is often a
glyph.

props.name: trigger
props.docs: What the trigger shows.

components.name: RowMenu
components.docs:
A row's secondary actions behind a "⋯" button.

Children are the actions, usually Ghost [`Button`]s. The panel is a plain
list of buttons and not `role="menu"`, which would promise arrow-key roving
that a script has to provide.

Choosing an action closes the menu. A native popover stays open on a click
inside it, so this one call goes through `document::eval`, as `Dialog`'s
`showModal()` does.

components.name: HelpTip
components.docs:
A "?" that opens a short explanation beside the thing it explains.

Help a reader needs in order to fill a field belongs in the field's own help
text; this is for the definition someone may want once.

props.name: label
props.docs: What the "?" explains, as its accessible name.

components.name: TimerReadout
components.docs:
A clock and, when there is a plan, the pace word beside it.

Children are the controls: start, pause, skip.

example.code: TimerReadout { label: "Section", elapsed_secs: 130, planned_secs: 120, direction: ClockDirection::Down }

components.name: SectionTimer
components.docs:
One section of a timed run: where it sits in the run, what to say, what
comes next, and its clock against its plan.

Children are the run controls.

props.name: section
props.docs: Zero-based.

components.name: BoundaryPill
components.docs:
A pill naming where an assistant runs. The boundary is in the words, not
only the colour.

example.code: BoundaryPill {}

components.name: GroundingNote
components.docs:
The line under a drafted answer saying what it was grounded in and where it
ran: "Grounded in 4 checklist facts · local only".

props.name: noun
props.docs: What was cited, plural.

example.code: GroundingNote { cited: 4, noun: "checklist facts" }

components.name: Blob
components.docs:
A jelly mascot, in SVG.

Poke it. It squashes, rebounds, and after enough pokes it has had enough —
`on_overpoke` fires, which is the hook for the joke.

Every colour is a CSS custom property (`--jelly-body`, `--jelly-cheek`,
`--jelly-eye`), so one component reskins per context by setting them on any
ancestor. That is upstream's design and it is the right one: a `color` prop
would need a variant per palette.

`gaze` nudges where it looks, in viewBox units. Pair it with a focused input
and the blob reads along as you type.

props.name: gaze
props.docs:
Where it looks, in viewBox units, clamped to a small range so the pupils
stay inside the eyes.

props.name: patience
props.docs: How many pokes it tolerates before `on_overpoke`.

components.name: Crumple
components.docs:
Wraps content that crumples up and disappears when `crumpled` flips.

The caller owns the flag, so the element can be removed from the tree after
the animation rather than lingering invisible — `on_done` is the hook.

components.name: Fur
components.docs:
A furry surface. Ruffles when hovered.

Layered `repeating-linear-gradient`s rather than an image: it costs no
request, scales to any size, and recolours from one custom property.

props.name: tint
props.docs: Base colour, any CSS colour.

components.name: GradientBuilder
components.docs:
An interactive gradient editor that emits the CSS.

This one is reproduced in full, because it is pure state — there is no
simulation to approximate, so nothing is lost in translation.

props.name: on_change
props.docs: Fires whenever the CSS changes, with the full `linear-gradient(...)`.

example.code: GradientBuilder {}

components.name: Hologram
components.docs:
A foil card that catches the light.

Tilts toward the pointer, the sheen tracks it, and the border glows where the
light is. With no pointer it keeps sweeping on its own, because a foil card
that is inert until touched looks like a bug.

**Honest about the gap:** upstream drives an SVG `feDiffuseLighting` bump map
off the card art and re-lights it per frame, plus a canvas particle system.
This is gradients and transforms — convincing, and not the same thing. The
relief and the particles are absent, not approximated.

props.name: intensity
props.docs: 0.0–1.0. How strongly the foil reads.

props.name: tilt
props.docs: Maximum tilt in degrees at the edges.

components.name: PullCord
components.docs:
A ceiling pull-cord.

Drag the knob down. It actuates **mid-pull**, the moment travel crosses
`actuation`, the way a real pull-chain detents — not on release. Let go and
it swings back and settles.

**Honest about the gap:** upstream simulates the rope, with gravity, damping
and stiffness you can tune, integrated per frame. This is a drag plus a
keyframed damped swing. It reads as a rope; it is not solving one. Doing it
properly needs a render loop, which this crate deliberately cannot have.

props.name: actuation
props.docs: Travel in pixels at which it actuates.

props.name: travel
props.docs: How far it can be dragged before it stops following.

components.name: Vacuum
components.docs:
Wraps content that gets sucked toward a point and vanishes.

`target` is the offset to travel, in CSS length units — aim it at wherever
the nozzle, bin or tab actually is.

types.name: Arrive
types.docs: How a magnitude mark appears.
variants: Static — At its length from the first paint.
Grow — Grows from its baseline while it enters the viewport.

types.name: BadgeFill
types.docs:
How a [`Badge`] without a category colour is filled.

An enum rather than a `class`, because the badge already sets a fill and a
text colour of its own, and a second pair passed in through `class` won or
lost against them by stylesheet order (UI5). A product page once relied on
that for every verdict chip it drew.
variants: Takeable — The thing labelled passes the reader's filter. Spent on nothing else.
Strong — The emphatic one of a pair, said with fill rather than a hue.
Quiet — The quiet one of the same pair: present, not asserted.
Tint — A count beside a heading or tab: the parent's text colour at low strength, so it re-tints with whatever it sits in.

types.name: Boundary
types.docs:
Where an assistant's work runs, as the reader is told it.

A kit-local enum: apps map `rv2_ai::DataBoundary` onto it, so the kit does
not depend on `rv2-ai` and a product without it can still say "on device".
variants: RemoteWithConsent — Sent to a remote model, with the reader's consent.
signatures: fn word(self) -> &'static str

types.name: Choice
types.docs: One option in a [`ChoiceGroup`].
signatures: fn new(value: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn hint(self, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: ClockDirection
types.docs: Which way a [`TimerReadout`] counts.
variants: Down — Time left; past zero it shows the overrun with a plus sign.

types.name: ColumnKind
types.docs: What a [`LedgerTable`] column holds.
variants: Figure — A number: end-aligned, tabular digits, never wrapped.

types.name: CompareRow
types.docs: One row of a [`CompareTable`]: what is compared, then one cell per option.
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, cells: Vec<String>) -> Self

types.name: Dated
types.docs: What a [`Citation`]'s date records.
variants: Captured — When the figure was copied from the source.
Checked — When the source was last read and still said this.
Published — When the source itself was published.
signatures: fn word(self) -> &'static str

types.name: DeleteClick
types.docs: What a click on an [`ArmedDeleteButton`] does next.
signatures: fn next(armed: bool) -> Self

types.name: Density
types.docs: How loud a [`StatStrip`] is.
variants: Compact — A summary row above a table or a form.
Hero — The band a page is about: figures at display size.

types.name: DialogKind
types.docs: Where a [`Dialog`] sits.
variants: Centered — Centred panel, for a decision.
Drawer — Full-height panel from the inline end, for a form or a detail view beside the list it came from.

types.name: Fact
types.docs: A `label → value` row, for cost breakdowns and spec tables.
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn total(label: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn chosen(label: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: FactWeight
types.docs: What a [`Fact`] row is in its sum.
variants: Total — The computed result: bold, under a rule.
Chosen — A figure someone set that stands in for the computed one — a quote beside the arithmetic that suggested it. Inverted, so it is never read as the sum.

types.name: Foil
types.docs: The foil pattern under the light.
variants: Sunburst — Rays from a point. The classic.
Cosmos — A swirl, for the cosmic ones.

types.name: FooterColumn
types.docs: A titled column of links in the [`Footer`].
signatures: fn new(title: impl Into<String>, items: Vec<NavLink>) -> Self

types.name: Gate
types.docs: One check in a [`GateList`].
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, verdict: Verdict) -> Self
fn detail(self, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: HeadingSize
types.docs:
Visual size of a [`Heading`], independent of its semantic level.

The three larger sizes set `font-display` and `font-heading`, which the
kit's theme points at the body family at semibold. An app with a display
face sets `--font-display` and `--font-weight-heading` and every heading
follows, instead of each call site spelling the family and weight.
variants: Title — The name of one entry in a list of them, or of a single item's page.

types.name: Lean
types.docs:
Which way a figure leans, for a reader deciding whether it is good news.

Said in colour **and** in a leading sign the caller writes into the value
(`+£120`, `−4 min`): colour alone is not a judgement anyone can act on.
variants: Good — Under budget, above the floor, ahead of time.
Close — Close to a limit, not over it.
Bad — Over budget, below the floor, behind.

types.name: LedgerCell
types.docs: One cell: its value, an optional second line, and the ink of the value.
signatures: fn new(value: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn note(mut self, note: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn lean(mut self, lean: Lean) -> Self
fn href(mut self, href: impl Into<String>) -> Self
impl<T: Into<String>> From<T> for LedgerCell

types.name: LedgerColumn
types.docs: One column of a [`LedgerTable`].
signatures: fn text(label: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn figure(label: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: LedgerRow
types.docs: One record of a [`LedgerTable`].
signatures: fn new(key: impl Into<String>, cells: Vec<LedgerCell>) -> Self
fn voided(mut self) -> Self
fn milestone(mut self) -> Self
fn action(mut self, action: Element) -> Self

types.name: Mood
types.docs: What the blob is feeling. Drives the eyes and mouth.
variants: Password — Eyes shut. For a password field — the blob is not looking.

types.name: NavLink
types.docs:
A link in the kit's navigation: a header route, a rail entry, a footer
link, a header call-to-action.

One record for all of them. There used to be three — `NavItem`,
`ProductNavItem` and `ProductHeaderAction` — each carrying the same label,
href and external flag with its own constructors, so a footer link and a
header link could not be the same value.

`key` is the stable route identity that `current` is matched against, so a
label or URL can change without breaking current-page state. A link that is
never "the current page" — a footer link, a call-to-action — has no key.
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, href: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn route(key: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>, href: impl Into<String>,) -> Self
fn external(self) -> Self

types.name: Pace
types.docs: Where a timed run stands against its plan.
variants: Closing — At or past the warning share of the plan.
signatures: fn word(self) -> &'static str

types.name: Pad
types.docs:
Inner spacing of a [`Card`].

Two values, because two is what the pages need: a list of cards that should
read as a list, and a single card that is the whole of its section. Hand-made
surfaces had been using four (`p-3`, `p-4`, `p-6`, `p-8`), which is the
drift and not a design. `None` is a card whose content brings its own edge —
a table running to the border.

types.name: Part
types.docs: One part of a [`SplitBar`].
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, amount: f64, readout: impl Into<String>, colour: impl Into<String>,) -> Self

types.name: PopoverAlign
types.docs: Which edge of its trigger a [`Popover`] lines up with.

types.name: PopoverRole
types.docs: What a [`Popover`]'s panel holds, which sets its role.
variants: Content — Controls or links; no role.
Note — An explanation the reader asked for: `role="note"`.

types.name: Press
types.docs: Which of the two tactile treatments a control takes.
variants: Primary — Ink fill on a deeper ledge. One per view: the action the page is for.
Soft — Soft fill with an edge. Everything else that still deserves a ledge.
Offset — Square, two-pixel ink border, hard diagonal shadow. The ledger look Logo Handoff, Talk Run Card, Sponsor Ledger and Solar Quote Check each drew by hand.

types.name: ProcessStep
types.docs: One stage in a [`ProcessRail`].
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, hint: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn linked(label: impl Into<String>, hint: impl Into<String>, href: impl Into<String>,) -> Self

types.name: QandA
types.docs: One question/answer pair.
signatures: fn new(question: impl Into<String>, answer: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: QueueItem
types.docs: One row of an [`AttentionQueue`].
signatures: fn go(id: impl Into<String>, title: impl Into<String>, reason: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>, href: impl Into<String>,) -> Self
fn state(id: impl Into<String>, title: impl Into<String>, reason: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>, verdict: Verdict,) -> Self

types.name: QueueTrail
types.docs: The end of a queue row.
variants: Go — The row is a link to where the work happens.
State — The row reports a state; nothing to follow.

types.name: RailLayout
types.docs: Which way a [`ProcessRail`] runs.
variants: Row — Steps side by side, two per row on a phone.
Column — Steps stacked: a timeline beside the content it tracks, or a stepper in a narrow column. Edit Scope's timeline and Reefdose's stepper.

types.name: ReasonStyle
types.docs: How a row's reason reads.
variants: Evidence — Measured evidence — "3 sessions missed" — in mono tabular digits.

types.name: Redline
types.docs: One changed field in a [`RedlineDiff`].
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, before: impl Into<String>, after: impl Into<String>,) -> Self

types.name: RowState
types.docs: What a [`LedgerRow`] is, beyond its figures.
variants: Voided — Kept for the record and no longer counted. Every cell says so in words to assistive technology, since a reader moving cell by cell may never hear the row header; on screen the cells after the header are struck through and the row drops to muted ink.
Milestone — A boundary in the run — a year end, a subtotal.

types.name: SegmentFlow
types.docs: How a [`SegmentedControl`] lays out its segments.
variants: Row — One joined row at every width.
StackNarrow — A joined column below `sm`, for labels too long to share a phone's row.

types.name: Size
types.docs: Control height.
variants: Small — Inline with dense content: a demo's controls, a toolbar of many.

types.name: Space
types.docs: Vertical rhythm between page sections.

types.name: Stat
types.docs: One cell of a [`StatStrip`].
signatures: fn new(label: impl Into<String>, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn note(self, note: impl Into<String>) -> Self
fn lean(self, lean: Lean) -> Self

types.name: StatusTone
types.docs:
How a [`Status`] reads at a glance.

Named apart from [`crate::typography::Tone`], which grades text emphasis
rather than health.
signatures: fn dot(self) -> &'static str
fn text(self) -> &'static str

types.name: Step
types.docs: One step of a numbered process.
signatures: fn new(title: impl Into<String>, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self

types.name: Surface
types.docs: The edge of a [`Card`].
variants: Flat — Hairline border, rounded, no shadow.
Slab — Square, a 2px ink border and a hard offset shadow: the printed-slab look of Logo Handoff, Talk Run Card, Sponsor Ledger and Solar Quote. Pairs with [`crate::Press::Offset`].

types.name: Tab
types.docs: One selectable tab.
signatures: fn new(value: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self

signatures: fn life_ms(&self) -> Option<u64>
fn assertive(&self) -> bool

types.docs: Raises and dismisses toasts. Copy it into any handler.
signatures: fn raise(self, verdict: Verdict, message: impl Into<String>) -> u64
fn raise_titled(self, verdict: Verdict, title: impl Into<String>, message: impl Into<String>,) -> u64
fn dismiss(self, id: u64)

types.docs: The toasts on screen, oldest first.
signatures: fn push(&mut self, verdict: Verdict, title: Option<String>, message: String) -> u64
fn dismiss(&mut self, id: u64)
fn toasts(&self) -> &[Toast]

types.name: Tone
types.docs:
Body text tone.

The tone owns the paragraph's colour, and a `class` passed to [`Text`]
cannot override it reliably: two colour utilities on one element resolve by
stylesheet order, not by which was written last. So a paragraph that needs
a different colour needs a tone, not a class (UI5). `OnInk` is the one that
was missing — secondary text on an ink-filled plate, which `apps/web` had
been writing by hand because `Text` kept painting it dark-on-dark.

types.name: Variant
types.docs:
Visual weight of a [`Button`] or [`LinkButton`].

`Outline` is the quiet secondary action — "Clear every filter", "Export CSV"
— that apps had been hand-writing as `rounded-md border border-rule …` seven
times. `Link` is a button that reads as a text link, for an action sitting
in running text where a filled control would shout; it is still a
`<button>`, because it does something rather than going somewhere.

types.name: Verdict
types.docs: What a [`Callout`] or [`Receipt`] is telling the reader.
variants: Note — Context worth reading; no judgement.
Clear — The check passed: it applies, it is ready, it is above the floor.
Caution — Not wrong, not finished: missing evidence, stale, open.
Stop — It does not apply, it failed, it is below the floor.

types.name: Width
types.docs:
Horizontal content width.

`Prose` is deliberately narrower than `Default`: long-form reading breaks
down past roughly 75 characters per line, so guide pages want a tighter
measure than a three-column card grid does.

`Narrow` is a single form — sign-in and the like — where a wider column only
stretches the inputs. `Dense` is a data screen that wants every column it can
get: a filter rail beside a results table. It also takes the smaller gutter,
because on such a screen the gutter is width the data does not get.

types.name: clock
types.docs: Seconds as `m:ss`, or `h:mm:ss` from an hour.
signatures: fn clock(secs: u32) -> String

types.name: command_matches
types.docs: Matches every search word against the visible label, retaining caller order.
signatures: fn command_matches(label: &str, query: &str) -> bool

types.name: command_step
types.docs: Arrow navigation wraps; an empty list never produces an option index.
signatures: fn command_step(current: usize, count: usize, previous: bool) -> Option<usize>

types.name: field_description
types.docs: IDs of the nonempty messages rendered by [`FieldShell`].
signatures: fn field_description(id: &str, help: Option<&str>, error: Option<&str>) -> Option<String>

types.docs:
The pace band for `elapsed` of `planned` seconds, closing from `warn_pct`
percent of the plan. Over means strictly past the plan.
signatures: fn pace(elapsed: u32, planned: u32, warn_pct: u8) -> Pace

types.docs:
SVG polyline points for `values` across `width` × `height`.

Empty when any value is not finite or the box is empty, so a broken series
draws nothing rather than a line through invented data. One value, or a
flat series, is a line across the middle.
signatures: fn spark_points(values: &[f64], width: f64, height: f64) -> String
